title: Provisional measurement review
notice: These are newly derived, unvalidated educational observations. The source supplies no printed answer key for this exercise. They are unscored and require qualified ECG educator review.

fields.basis: Visually checked ventricular landmarks on original PDF 521
fields.reason: Successive ventricular peak spacings: 138 px, 137 px, 138 px, 139 px, 137 px. Descriptive judgment from visible spacing, not a validated diagnostic threshold.

fields.basis: Course-standard 25 mm/s assumption; 150 independently detected small-square intervals across 738 pixels
fields.reason: Mean R–R estimate 53.6 bpm; six-second count estimate 60 bpm. All seconds/bpm depend on course-standard 25 mm/s. Count estimate assumes 150 small squares = 6 seconds; endpoint phase and partial complexes affect it. On irregular strips the count estimate is not a stable instantaneous rate. Mean RR describes only intervals between observed peaks.

fields.value: Candidate P-wave observation: Tiny rounded pre-complex bumps recur, separated from the substantially larger broad post-complex waves. Their small height, shallow onset and baseline thickness limit identification as atrial activity.
fields.basis: Original PDF page 521; independently reconciled selected-complex observation
fields.reason: Provisional deflection description, not validated atrial identity or a diagnosis. Describes visible morphology/association only, not established P identity, atrial origin or conduction. Are the tiny pre-complex bumps atrial P waves rather than baseline texture? Does QRS end at the terminal notch return or slightly later shelf? This describes only the selected complexes or restricted subset. It does not establish a whole-strip event census, ventricular sequence completeness, atrial identity, or conduction relationship. Qualified ECG educator review is outstanding.

fields.basis: Original PDF page 521; independently reconciled endpoint bands and horizontal grid; assumes course 25 mm/s (0.04 s per small square), not a verified per-strip speed
fields.reason: Propose broad conditional envelope: sharp positive complexes return through a small terminal negative notch to a relatively flat shelf. The offset band includes the notch recovery. Assumes course 25 mm/s and correct component identity/boundaries. Envelopes describe measurement uncertainty, not actual duration variability. Are the tiny pre-complex bumps atrial P waves rather than baseline texture? Does QRS end at the terminal notch return or slightly later shelf? This describes only the selected complexes or restricted subset. It does not establish a whole-strip event census, ventricular sequence completeness, atrial identity, or conduction relationship. This envelope includes reader and endpoint uncertainty; it is not a confidence interval, normal/abnormal classification, or proof of beat-to-beat physiological variation. Qualified ECG educator review is outstanding.

fields.value: Approximately regular ventricular spacing, about 54 bpm by conditional mean RR versus about 60 bpm by the short-strip count. These are different short-sample summaries, not interchangeable evidence for a rate-category boundary. Tiny pre-complex candidates do not establish P identity or PR, and the conditional QRS envelope does not settle width. A sinus or escape origin cannot be selected from rate alone.
fields.basis: New independently reviewed educational synthesis of the exact original raster, conditional source measurements and stated course criteria; not a source-authored or educator-validated rhythm answer
fields.reason: Qualified ECG educator review has not occurred. Visible-deflection observations are supplied without validated P-wave identity. QRS has an unvalidated conditional estimate; numeric PR remains withheld. Optional educational comparison only, not a source-authored answer or confirmed rhythm diagnosis. A candidate atrial association is not proof of sinus origin. Timing retains the recorded calibration assumptions and holds. Interval envelopes apply to the selected endpoint-review cycles and describe boundary uncertainty, not actual beat-to-beat variability, normal conduction or a full-strip atrial census. These newly derived observations remain unscored and are not eligible as validated answer keys.

limitations: Wave observations and conditional endpoint envelopes remain provisional and unscored. QT/QTc, calibrated amplitudes and clinical diagnosis are not established. Selected-complex widths do not establish sequence certainty.

pr unresolved: Hold PR: a repeatable candidate hump is visible, but its onset is at roughly the same vertical scale as baseline thickness. Record exploratory onset-to-onset bands rather than treat it as an identified P wave.

P-wave text is a provisional description, not validated atrial identity. PR remains unresolved with no numerical answer. QRS has an unvalidated conditional endpoint envelope for selected complexes. Validated electrical boundaries and qualified educator adjudication remain outstanding.
Calibration assumes the course’s 25 mm/s convention, not speed metadata printed on each strip. Peak uncertainty is approximately ±2 source pixels, excluding errors in identifying the waveform.
